skill.name: webask-workspace-access
skill.description: Управляет участниками аккаунта WebAsk и их правами: приглашения, роли, доступ к папкам. Применяется, когда человек хочет дать коллеге доступ, ограничить его или разобраться, почему участник не видит нужные опросы.
skill.summary: Manage WebAsk invitations, roles, and folder permissions through MCP tools, with guidance for diagnosing missing access and avoiding excessive privileges.
skill.author: webaskio

security_audit.summary: All 13 static findings are false positives: one documentation navigation link and twelve Markdown references to MCP tools. No evidence found of prompt injection, unauthorized data transfer, or shell execution in the reviewed files. The skill guides legitimate permission changes and includes safeguards against excessive privileges, unsolicited member removal, and deleting assigned roles.

content.value_statement: Missing folder permissions and unaccepted invitations can prevent colleagues from seeing surveys. This skill guides WebAsk MCP tools to inspect access and apply task-specific permissions.
actual_capabilities: Guides inspection of WebAsk workspaces, members, roles, and individual access through MCP tools.
Supports inviting members and resending invitations through the corresponding MCP tools.
Guides role assignment and folder access changes based on each member's tasks.
Explains missing survey access caused by unaccepted invitations, inaccessible folders, or restrictions to personally created surveys.
Supports member removal only after an explicit request and warns that returning requires a new invitation.
Guides role creation, updates, and deletion, with instructions to check assignments before deleting a role.
limitations: Requires configured WebAsk MCP tools and sufficient account permissions; the skill does not implement the service.
Cannot accept invitations on behalf of invited members.
Member removal requires a new invitation to restore membership.
Does not resolve account plan limits; it instructs the assistant to report the limit and stop.

use_cases.title: Onboard a colleague
use_cases.description: Invite a colleague and select the role and folders required for their work after inspecting existing access.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing surveys
use_cases.description: Check invitation acceptance, assigned roles, and folder permissions when a colleague cannot see expected surveys.

use_cases.title: Review excessive permissions
use_cases.description: Compare member permissions with job tasks and identify where results-only access would be sufficient.

prompt_templates.title: List current access
prompt_templates.prompt: Show members and roles in [workspace]. Do not change any permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate missing surveys
prompt_templates.prompt: Check why [member] cannot see surveys in [folder] within [workspace]. Inspect invitation status and permissions, then explain the cause without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Invite with limited access
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect roles in [workspace], then propose results-only access to [folder] for [email]. Ask me to confirm the role and folder before sending the invitation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: onboard a colleague with limited privileges.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a permission review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review roles and folder access in [workspace] against [team responsibilities]. Propose minimal permissions and identify assigned roles before suggesting deletion. Make no changes without confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review access across a team.

output_examples.input: In this example, a colleague has an Analyst role but no assigned folders. Why is the survey list empty?
output_examples.output: The role does not provide access to the needed folders. Grant only the relevant folder access after confirming the colleague's task.

output_examples.input: In this example, an invited colleague appears in the member list but has not accepted the invitation.
output_examples.output: The pending invitation does not provide access yet. The colleague must accept it; the invitation can be resent when requested.

output_examples.input: A colleague has full access but only needs to view results. What should I review?
output: Check the current role and folder access.
Select a role without editing privileges and retain only the required folders.
Do not remove the member unless explicitly requested.

best_practices: Inspect the selected workspace, member access, and roles before proposing changes.
Choose permissions from the member's actual tasks and grant only the required folders.
Confirm consequential changes and check role assignments before deleting any role.
anti_patterns: Granting full access merely to make a missing survey visible.
Removing a member without an explicit request.
Deleting a role before checking which members use it.

faq.question: What must be configured before using this skill?
faq.answer: The assistant needs access to the listed WebAsk MCP tools and an account authorized for the requested operations.

faq.question: Why does an invited member still lack access?
faq.answer: The member must accept the invitation. Appearing in the member list alone does not mean access is active.

faq.question: Why can a member have a role but see no surveys?
faq.answer: The required folders may be inaccessible. A restriction to personally created surveys can also limit visibility.

faq.question: Can this skill change roles and folder permissions?
faq.answer: It guides the corresponding WebAsk MCP tools, subject to account authorization. It recommends inspecting existing access and granting only needed permissions.

faq.question: Can a removed member simply be restored?
faq.answer: The skill states that a removed member must receive a new invitation. It prohibits removal without an explicit request.

faq.question: What happens when an account limit prevents an action?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to explain the limit and stop, without recommending a plan change or directing the user to payment.
